title: A Data-centric Framework to Endow Graph Neural Networks with Out-Of-Distribution Detection Ability

problem.claim: Out-of-distribution detection identifies OOD samples from ID samples at test time.

gap.claim: Graph-structured OOD detection remains under-explored, and existing graph OOD methods require retraining a GNN from scratch at high computational cost.

contributions.claim: AAGOD is a post-hoc, data-centric framework that adds graph OOD detection ability to a well-trained GNN without modifying its parameters.
AAGOD superimposes a parameterized amplifier matrix on each input graph's adjacency matrix and reuses the well-trained GNN to encode the amplified graph for scoring.
The framework includes a Learnable Amplifier Generator for graph-specific amplifiers and a Regularized Learning Strategy requiring no OOD data.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the work as the first attempt to endow a well-trained GNN with OOD detection ability without modifying its parameters.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that AAGOD can be applied to various GNNs to enable OOD detection.
Against the stated state-of-the-art graph OOD baseline, the authors report a 6.21% average relative AUC enhancement and 34-times faster training.
The authors report that code and data are available.

narrative_sequence.summary: OOD detection is important, while graph-structured OOD detection is under-explored.
Existing graph OOD approaches require costly GNN retraining from scratch.
AAGOD reuses a well-trained GNN by applying learned amplifier matrices to input graph adjacency matrices.
Graph-specific amplifiers are generated by LAG and trained with RLS without OOD data.
The authors report applicability across GNNs, improved AUC, and faster training than a stated baseline.

source_observation.claim: AAGOD manipulates input graph structure while keeping the pretrained GNN parameters unchanged.

interpretation.claim: Post-hoc data-centric adaptation can potentially reuse existing model representations for a new detection capability.

application.claim: When retraining is costly, consider adapting inputs or representations around a pretrained model before changing its parameters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when input amplification may fail or be unsuitable.

unknowns: Datasets, experimental settings, and metric definitions are not specified.
The abstract does not detail the amplifier architecture, scoring functions, or regularization objective.
